overview: Brooklyn Collaborative is committed to developing students and staff who are kind, openminded, persistent, responsible, and courageous. Our students and our curriculum reflect the city we live in. We are committed to being diverse with regard to race, ethnicity, socio-economics, religion, and academics. Our students see themselves and their communities represented widely in the history they study, the books and texts they read, and the expeditions they engage in. Our students use the city as their classroom. Fieldwork is a regular part of learning at Brooklyn Collaborative: students regularly meet with experts, tour neighborhoods and museums, analyze artifacts, collect lab samples, and more. We are committed to developing the social and emotional self as well as the academic self through Crew. In crew (a daily advisory class), students learn to be agents of self-change, to take responsibility for their learning, and to develop supportive relationships with adults and peers. We are a Grades 6-12 school with a 100% college acceptance rate and a NYS Regents waiver. Our major partners are NYC Outward Bound and the New York Performance Standards Consortium.There's something for everyone at BCS!

overview: The Brooklyn School of Inquiry programs are designed to foster self-directed learning by encouraging exploration, inquiry and reflective thinking. We are a K-8, citywide gifted and talented school, rooted in the principles of inquiry-based learning and progressive education. We emphasize STEAM education, literacy development, play-based learning and social and emotional development. The 2017-2018 school year marked the beginning of the Diversity in Admissions program and 40% of our incoming kindergarten class is eligible for free or reduced price lunch. We are not a zoned, community school and 85% of our students are bussed to the school by either the Office of Pupil Transportation or private busses that are funded by the families that use them. We are deeply committed to a strong sense of community rooted in the Tribes Agreements, Responsive Classroom approaches and our middle school advisory program. We feel strongly that student choice allows for positive growth and development, therefore during the school day, we offer lunch clubs, elective courses and our students engage in a variety of after school programs such as debate, band, robotics, musical theater and art and math clubs. We have a state-of-the-art rooftop STEM lab where all students study hydroponics, aquaponics and other environmental science topics.

overview: Global Innovators Academy (MS 428), located in Sunset Park, is a dual-language middle school in District 15. As a trailblazing school grounded in project-based learning, we are committed to cultivating the next generation of compassionate global citizens who are bilingual, biliterate, and bicultural. Our mission is to harness the power of language, rigorous academics, and cross-cultural collaboration to prepare students for an ever-evolving world. We strive to foster a safe and inclusive learning environment that values each individual’s strengths, identity, culture, and heritage, while building a harmonious and diverse community. At MS 428, we prioritize high academic achievement through an equitable, culturally responsive curriculum enriched with integrated project-based learning. Students engage in meaningful opportunities to collaborate with diverse populations through workshops and community-centered projects that promote real-world impact. A hallmark of our school model is our innovative approach to language learning. We provide interdisciplinary instruction by embedding community service and project-based experiences into the core curriculum, empowering students to apply their language skills in authentic and meaningful ways. Through thoughtful scheduling and a high-quality, inclusive curriculum, we ensure that all learners-regardless of background have equitable access to opportunities that prepare them for college, career, and beyond. Opening in September 2024, Global Innovators Academy welcomes students who are inspired by an immersive dual-language experience and eager to grow as leaders. Our students actively participate in community-building initiatives that cultivate leadership, global awareness, and the skills needed to thrive in the world of tomorrow.

overview:

At Dewey, we are committed to creating a safe, inclusive, and supportive learning environment where every student feels valued, challenged, and empowered. We believe in educating the whole child and preparing students to thrive in high school, college, careers, and beyond.

overview: At MS 88, every student is known, valued, and inspired. We are a welcoming, innovative middle school where students discover their passions, develop their voice, and build the confidence and skills for future success. Beginning in Fall 2026, MS 88 launches a redesigned middle school experience that combines rigorous academics, student choice, and real-world learning within smaller learning communities where students develop meaningful relationships, a strong sense of belonging, and the personalized support to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. All sixth graders begin in our Discovery Academy, a supportive transition program focused on executive functioning, organization, leadership, and independence while exploring both the Creative Conservatory (Arts) and Innovation Institute (STEM) through immersive electives and project-based learning. At the end of sixth grade, students choose a pathway that aligns with their interests. The Creative Conservatory nurtures artistic expression through visual arts, music, theater, and performance, while the Innovation Institute immerses students in coding, robotics, engineering, artificial intelligence, health sciences, digital media, and design thinking. Across all grades, students develop critical thinking, communication, collaboration, creativity, and leadership through authentic learning, capstone experiences, and community partnerships. With accelerated coursework, comprehensive supports, and exceptional programs in athletics, robotics, theater, music, visual arts, and student leadership, MS 88 empowers every learner to become an innovative thinker, compassionate leader, and engaged citizen prepared to thrive in high school, college, careers, and beyond.

overview:
Montauk Junior High School: Empowering Future Leaders in a Diverse and Nurturing Environment
Montauk Junior High School is a vibrant, inclusive learning community serving approximately 650 students who represent over 17 languages. Our small school environment allows us to provide personalized attention and foster strong relationships between students, teachers, and families. With a low student-to-teacher ratio and a commitment to academic excellence, we are proud to offer a wide range of programs that challenge and support our diverse learners.
Academic Excellence and Opportunity
Montauk JHS provides a robust academic program, including accelerated and Regents-level courses. Students in select classes take Algebra and Biology, with over 95% of students passing these Regents exams annually. As the host site for District Algebra Honors and Superintendent Classes, we provide accelerated pathways for students to earn high school credits in 8th grade. These include Regents exams in Algebra, Biology, U.S. History, and the Language Proficiency Exam in Mandarin.
We are also proud to offer the AVID program, a nationally recognized college and career readiness initiative, which equips students with essential study skills and prepares them for rigorous coursework in high school and beyond.
Real-World Readiness: Financial Literacy and Civics for All
In preparing students for life beyond the classroom, Montauk JHS prioritizes Financial Literacy and Civics Education for all students. Our curriculum includes dedicated instruction in money management, budgeting, and financial responsibility, ensuring that every student gains essential life skills. Additionally, through the Civics for All initiative, students engage in meaningful exploration of civic duties.

overview: William McKinley IS 259, a Title 1 middle school in Brooklyn Bay Ridge, serves grades 6-8 with rigorous academics including screened Independent Investigations Method (IIM) and Virtual Enterprises Junior Ventures (VEJV) programs, a Mandarin Dual Language program, and Regents-tracked coursework in Algebra, Living Environment, and U.S. History available to all students. Acceptance into the Virtual Enterprise and/or Independent Investigations Method programs will limit a student's scheduling options for certain other electives. However, we offer nearly all electives after school (and many before school) for students who do not have room in their daytime schedule but still wish to participate. Students benefit from two upgraded air-conditioned gyms, Promethean Interactive Boards and laptops in every classroom, state-of-the-art auditorium lighting and sound, and hands-on science labs with major upgrades. The school offers a robust Visual and Performing Arts program, including Advanced String Orchestra and Marching Band, along with a wide range of extracurriculars such as robotics, culinary arts, sports, student government, and leadership clubs. McKinley emphasizes social-emotional wellness and community engagement through after-school programs, parent involvement, and partnerships with local organizations, preparing students to be bilingual, biliterate, and bicultural global citizens ready for high school and beyond. At BHS, students are encouraged to take intellectual risks, explore their passions, engage with diverse perspectives, and become active contributors to their communities. Our mission is simple: Every Child is Our Child.

Our Exploration Program is an outgrowth of our school's philosophy: middle school students are social individuals and benefit from learning through cooperative groups. The Exploration experience provides students with the opportunity to get off-site and explore city-wide educational institutions. Students have arts (music, theater, dance, visual art, and technology) for all three years. Our advisory program supports students' academic, social, and emotional learning, and we employ restorative practices across our school. Our free after-school program allows students to learn new skills and share common interests, through sports, arts, and leadership. We have earned a Blackboard Award for Outstanding School in Brooklyn and consistent excellent ratings on the School Quality Snapshot.

overview: The Urban Assembly School for Leadership and Empowerment is a small 6-12 school that prepares young female, transgender, and non-binary students for success in college and the world of work. We provide an academically rigorous curriculum that reflects the core set of knowledge and skills necessary for students to become culturally literate problem solvers, capable of becoming leaders in their local and global community. Embracing the theme of empowerment through social equity and activism, we develop our students into critical thinkers who rely on evidence, logic, and sound reasoning to formulate ideas and to support them. Our school, in collaboration with community stakeholders, supports students as they transition into adulthood in an environment which fosters the emotional, physical and intellectual growth necessary for post- secondary independence. All of our 8th graders take two Regents courses, Biology and Algebra I, setting them up with HS credits and advanced placement before entering high school. Our students are part of a tight-knit, diverse community and they benefit greatly from our small size and unique personal attention, with many opportunities for leadership and meaningful student-adult partnerships. Every student is placed in an advisory that focuses on Social Emotional Learning. Affinity spaces are available for students who identify in various identity groups. Restorative Justice and Peer Mediation are a big part of our community values and norms and our staff embraces anti-racism, social justice and equity in our classrooms + community.
